sections.content: How many people are "stock control clerks and assistants"?

66,640 people

were counted on the census as "stock control clerks and assistants" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Stock control clerks and assistants receive orders from customers, prepare requisitions or despatch documents for ordered goods, maintain and update records, files and other correspondence in relation to the storage and despatch of goods.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "stock control clerks and assistants" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "stock control clerks and assistants", 13.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "stock control clerks and assistants" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "stock control clerks and assistants" included:

  • transport and distribution clerks and assistants
  • food, drink and tobacco process operatives
  • legal associate professionals

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "stock control clerks and assistants" there were more men than women (58.1% compared with 41.9%).

This means "stock control clerks and assistants" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "administrative occupations".

Men made up 58.1% and women made up 41.9% of "stock control clerks and assistants"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "stock control clerks and assistants" included:

  • natural and social science professionals (other)
  • arts officers, producers and directors
  • specialist medical practitioners

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "stock control clerks and assistants" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "stock control clerks and assistants" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "stock control clerks and assistants", 9.2% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (79.8% compared with 20.2%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (96.7%) than self-employed (3.3%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
